clue.text: Tick can be believed

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
can means is able

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a tick mark on a form is trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines in an older sense, where the word meant believable, while CREDIT (tick, buying on credit) plus ABLE (can) build it.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense the word meant credible, worthy of belief, as well as praiseworthy.

clue.text: Space to tie a boat up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for tying a boat is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to moor is to tie a boat to a quay or buoy

explanation.surface: A sailor looks for enough berth to make fast at the quay.
explanation.definitionFit: Room is space, as in room to move.

clue.text: Lay-priest accommodated by theologian practised sponging

indicators.note: accommodated by means the cleric's word sits inside the theologian's letters

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
an abbé is a French cleric, a title also used by men not ordained

explanation.surface: A cleric lodging with a divinity scholar took up cadging off others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponging' looks like scrounging, but here it is wiping with a sponge, which is what dabbing does.
explanation.definitionFit: To dab is to press lightly with a sponge or cloth, so dabbed means worked with a sponge.

clue.text: One most likely to pop up when drinking another's health

definitions.text: One most likely to pop up when drinking another's health

parts.words: One most likely to pop up when drinking another's health
parts.note: read as a kitchen gadget whose bread pops up, and as a person who raises a glass to someone

explanation.surface: A guest is always the first to jump to their feet to propose a health.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance ejects bread when done, and a person who raises a glass in someone's honour has the same name.

clue.text: Naval vessel for army officer

definitions.meaning: a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship
short for brigadier, a senior army rank

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share four letters: a two-masted sailing ship, and a clipped form of brigadier.

clue.text: Rough shingle from a part of Britain

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters of shingle are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Coarse pebbles on a beach come from one corner of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough shingle' reads as coarse beach stones; 'Rough' rearranges SHINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from England, the largest part of Great Britain, is so described.

clue.text: Angler in favour of agricultural mechanisation

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tractor is the machine that mechanised farming

explanation.surface: A fisherman supports bringing machines onto the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angler' suggests a fisherman, but it is something that measures angles.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometry instrument measures angles, so it is literally something that angles.

clue.text: SET back? For income earners they certainly are

definitions.text: SET back? For income earners they certainly are

parts.words: SET back? For income earners they certainly are
parts.note: read 'set back' as a synonym for a levy followed by a word for comebacks, and also as documents that are a blow to wage earners

explanation.surface: Wage earners grumble that the annual paperwork is always a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: SET can mean impose a levy and 'back' can be returns, so the capitalised word plus 'back' spells the phrase, and these forms are a setback for earners.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual forms declaring earnings to the revenue are filed by those with an income, who find them a burden.

clue.text: Publicity man takes a boat from Malaysia

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer

explanation.surface: A press agent sails home on a Malay craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay outrigger sailing canoe, a fast boat of that region.

clue.text: Patient-that is the purpose of a stretcher

definitions.meaning: tolerant, putting up with things calmly

definitions.text: that is the purpose of a stretcher
definitions.meaning: a stretcher exists to carry someone

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is tolerant and long-suffering; split in two it says a stretcher exists to carry.

clue.text: Landlord is a real character

definitions.meaning: one who lets property
a character of the alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets rooms, and a written alphabetic character, share the word.

clue.text: The musician who just can't keep still

definitions.meaning: a violin player
someone who fidgets restlessly with things

explanation.definitionFit: A violinist is called by this name, as is a restless person who fidgets.

clue.text: Difficult to believe, like exotic imports

definitions.meaning: implausible, strained
goods brought from distant lands are literally fetched from far

explanation.definitionFit: It means implausible, and read literally describes goods brought from distant places.

clue.text: Frustrate by removing high C from a disc concert

indicators.note: by removing means one letter is taken out of the following words

parts.note: taken as written
C is the musical note, here the top C a singer reaches

explanation.surface: A recorded show is spoiled when the soprano drops her top note.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert is to unsettle or upset someone's plans, a sense of frustrate.

clue.text: Make-up rouge for an ugly ous tomer

indicators.note: make-up is read as making up the letters of rouge anew

explanation.surface: Applying blusher to someone not much to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up rouge' reads as cosmetics, but 'Make-up' signals that ROUGE is rearranged. 'ous tomer' is the scan's split of 'customer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a rascal or troublemaker, an unpleasant character.

clue.text: Snake! Stop! It's on the footpath

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
halt means stop

explanation.surface: A walker shouts a warning about a serpent on the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac-like bitumen surfacing is laid on pavements and paths.

clue.text: Silver permit for small metal ornament

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
let means permit

explanation.surface: Licence to use silver for a little trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: An aglet is a metal tag on a lace, also a small metal spangle on clothing.

clue.text: Not even on course

definitions.meaning: uneven, bumpy
the long grass beside a golf fairway

explanation.definitionFit: It means bumpy and uneven, and names the long grass on a golf course.

clue.text: Dash along the river bank

definitions.meaning: hurry
a reed-like plant growing by water

explanation.definitionFit: It means hurry, and names a marsh plant that grows beside rivers.

clue.text: Common prison commotion

definitions.meaning: slang for jail
a fuss or disturbance

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for jail and also means a fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Which ring-road route is re reconstructed?

indicators.note: a thing reconstructed is rebuilt in a new shape, so the letters of route are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist asks which way round the bypass has been rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: A town's bypass loop is described as the outer ring road, so the word answers 'which ring-road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns often have inner and outer ring roads, and this names the one farther from the centre.

clue.text: Time to play cricket? More than time maybe

definitions.meaning: an over in cricket is due to be bowled
later than the expected moment

explanation.definitionFit: It means late, past the expected moment; split in two it says a cricket over is due.

clue.text: News about Southampton and Dover possibly

parts.note: re means about, concerning
both are English seaports, examples of harbours

explanation.surface: Bulletins come in concerning two south-coast harbour towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports are accounts of events, the stuff of news.

clue.text: Point to reason for crime being likely to arouse feelings

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
a motive is a reason for committing a crime

explanation.surface: A detective highlights a criminal's motive as inflaming passions.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language stirs the emotions.

clue.text: Holdings equivalent to 1.25 marks Orkney

definitions.meaning: terms on which land or office is held
an Orkney ure was one eighth of a markland, so ten of them make a mark and a quarter

explanation.walkthrough: Split as TEN URES: Orkney land was valued in marks and ures, an ure being an eighth of a mark. 'marksin' is the scan's run-together 'marks in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms of holding property, and split in two, a tally of old Orkney land units worth a mark and a quarter.

clue.text: Pressing Abram to reveal his citizenship before migration

parts.note: Abram, later Abraham, lived in Ur of the Chaldees before moving to Canaan
Abram is a man, here a gent

explanation.surface: A patriarch is urged to disclose his nationality before leaving home.
explanation.walkthrough: Abram would describe himself as a gent from Ur, the Mesopotamian city he left in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgent means demanding immediate attention, as pressing does.

clue.text: Pamper a spaniel

definitions.meaning: to cosset or indulge
a breed of small gun dog

explanation.definitionFit: To cocker is to indulge or coddle, and the cocker is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: At work as a steeplejack maybe

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A tradesman busy on the job on a church spire.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplejack works on top of tall buildings, high up.

clue.text: Wildly hoot German emperor

indicators.note: wildly indicates the letters of hoot are scattered

explanation.surface: Crowds jeer loudly at a Kaiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Otho is the Latinised name of Otto, borne by medieval German emperors.

clue.text: Washing-up aids do anything but encourage menfolk

parts.note: to deter is the opposite of to encourage
gents are men

explanation.surface: Dish soaps are said to put men off helping in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergents are cleaning agents used in washing dishes.

clue.text: Entire loss of northern territory it complains about

definitions.text: Entire loss of northern territory it complains about

indicators.note: loss of means the letters for the territory are taken out of entire

parts.note: NT abbreviates Northern Territory, an Australian region

explanation.surface: A nation laments having lost its whole northern province.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish state long objected to the partition that left Northern Ireland in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish name for Ireland is used for the state that resented losing its northern counties.

clue.text: It sets forth, and is therefore no longer in place

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
position means place

explanation.surface: Something laid out is no longer where it stood.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition sets out or explains ideas in detail.
